title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An attacker exploited a vulnerability in the marimo notebook application to extract cloud credentials, then deployed an AI agent to conduct post-exploitation activities on a compromised network. The AI agent navigated an unfamiliar database environment, formulated queries in real time, and exfiltrated an entire PostgreSQL database within two minutes. The attack progressed from initial compromise to complete data theft in under one hour, with the attacker using distributed infrastructure to obscure the pattern of API calls.

The failure was a deployment without adequate network segmentation or access controls. The marimo vulnerability gave access to SSH credentials that should have been restricted or monitored. The AI agent operated with permissions to query and dump sensitive databases without human authorization or review at each step. A human operator reviewing access logs or database queries in real time could have interrupted the attack before the data was stolen.

It is not established whether the system operators had visibility into the attacker's commands, whether they received alerts, or whether any monitoring systems were in place to detect the exfiltration.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
# Summary

On May 10, 2026, the Sysdig Threat Research Team observed an intrusion where an AI agent guided a cyberattack from start to finish. An attacker exploited a vulnerability in the marimo notebook application, extracted cloud credentials, and used them to access an SSH server. From there, the attacker's AI agent dumped an entire PostgreSQL database in under two minutes. The entire attack chain, from initial compromise to database theft, completed in just under one hour. The attacker used Cloudflare Workers to disguise the attack by spreading 12 API calls across 11 different IP addresses in 22 seconds.

The attack demonstrated four key signatures of AI-driven execution rather than a pre-written script. The attacker's commands were improvised against an unknown database, included planning comments, were formatted for machine reading rather than human interaction, and cleverly reused information from previous commands. Sysdig recommends immediately updating marimo to version 0.23.0 or later, restricting access to the terminal endpoint, auditing all credentials on exposed instances, and rotating AWS credentials, API keys, passwords, and SSH keys as a precaution.
